title: paged-kv-cache: allocator reuse and locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Iris Park
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager has been a hotspot under high-concurrency streaming workloads. Allocator churn and indiscriminate pinning increased fragmentation and cross-NUMA traffic, degrading p99 latency and throughput. This PR implements allocator reuse and a locality-aware pinning strategy to reduce fragmentation, lower memory churn, and improve cache hit tail latencies.

Changes: 1) Block allocator reuse: introduce a fast freelist per-size-class to recycle recently freed blocks without returning them to the global allocator. The freelist is thread-local friendly and avoids expensive mutex grabs in the hot path. 2) Locality-aware pinning: blocks allocated for an active sequence are preferentially pinned to the same device NUMA region when possible, with a fallback heuristic that balances reuse and memory pressure. 3) Pinning TTL + gentle eviction: add a short TTL for pins so stale sequences don't keep blocks indefinitely; combined with LRU buckets to prioritize eviction of cold entries. 4) Metrics & tracing: expose allocator reuse rate, pin locality hit ratio, and per-device fragmentation counters. 5) Tests & benchmarks: microbenchmarks for allocation latency, end-to-end perf canary runs for streaming workloads, and integration tests covering pin expiration and eviction.

Performance: On the internal perf-canary suite (GPT-like streaming workload, 512 token average), results show: - 18% higher sustained throughput under 95th percentile concurrent streams - 12% reduction in p99 token latency - 28% reduction in lock contention stalls in the allocator hot path - 9% reduction in memory usage attributed to lower fragmentation. Benchmarks run across t4g/rtx6000-equivalent nodes and a dedicated multi-GPU dedicated cluster.

Compatibility & rollout: Changes are backwards-compatible at the config level. New pinning behavior is opt-in via a runtime flag (kv.pinning.locality_enabled) and pin TTL defaults to 30s. The rollout plan: staged canary -> dedicated clusters -> global. Feature gate and telemetry allow safe rollback.

Testing: Unit tests added for allocator freelist edge cases, pin TTL expiry, and eviction ordering. Integration tests added to the existing perf-canary harness. CI includes deterministic allocator race tests (flaky guard added), and benchmark job artifacts attached.

Related: ENG-4921 (paged-KV fragmentation), ENG-5098 (streaming p99 regressions), references previous block-manager PRs for allocator reuse and pinning heuristics.

review_comments: Rajesh Kumar: Can we avoid adding a global mutex hotspot when freelist is empty? Suggest per-device fallback and documented complexity tradeoffs.
Iris Park (author): Addressed - implemented per-size-class per-device freelist with a lock-free fast path and a fallback protected by a low-contention mutex. Added comments and benchmarks.
Eleanor Wu: The pin TTL default seems aggressive for long-running sessions; can we make it configurable per-tenant?
Iris Park: Agreed, exposed kv.pinning.ttl_seconds as a runtime config; default remains 30s but enterprise configs can increase this per-tenant.
Ben Thompson: Please add a regression test that simulates NUMA migration (synthetic) to validate locality heuristics.
Iris Park: Added a synthetic integration test that pins allocation to a fake device topology and asserts locality hit ratio improvements.
release_notes: Improved paged KV cache allocator (reduced fragmentation, lower p99 latency) and locality-aware pinning. Opt-in via kv.pinning.locality_enabled; pin TTL default 30s configurable at runtime. Recommended for streaming-heavy workloads.
